definition: In the fields of computational linguistics and applied linguistics, a morphological dictionary is a linguistic resource that contains correspondences between surface form and lexical forms of words.
details: Surface forms of words are those found in natural language text. The corresponding lexical form of a surface form is the lemma followed by grammatical information (for example the part of speech, gender and number). In English give, gives, giving, gave and given are surface forms of the verb give. The lexical form would be "give", verb. There are two kinds of morphological dictionaries: morpheme-aligned dictionaries and full-form (non-aligned) dictionaries.

explainer.lead: A morphological dictionary is a linguistic resource mapping surface forms of words to their lexical forms. It supplies the grammatical information that raw text lacks.

tiers.eli5: It is a lookup list that says which dictionary word a written word belongs to and what grammar goes with it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to link text tokens to lemmas plus grammatical tags. A pitfall is that surface forms are many while lexical forms are few, so coverage of forms must be handled.
tiers.paperLevel: Contains correspondences between surface form and lexical form, where the lexical form is the lemma followed by grammatical information such as part of speech, gender, and number; two kinds exist: morpheme-aligned and full-form (non-aligned) dictionaries.

explainer.example: The English surface forms give, gives, giving, gave, and given map to the lexical form "give", verb.
